answer: Before an agent can vote, a peer issues a raven challenge: solve a fresh 40-million-FLOP matrix kernel and return the result within a 900-millisecond wall-clock deadline, tight enough that one GPU cannot interleave two identities without blowing latency. The verifier timestamps the first and last token of the return stream, then checks the numerical delta against its own recomputation. Cloning fails because a shared GPU time-slices execution, stretching the delta past deadline; a nectar of forged identities cannot buy real concurrency.
